summary: A dice-drafting spin-off of Rajas of the Ganges that strips out the board and shrinks the whole game onto a scoresheet where players race to make their fame and money tracks intersect. It plays fast and light, with most of the tension coming from clever dice allocation and combo timing rather than long-term strategy.
praised: Fast, portable, and easy to teach compared to the original board game
Satisfying dice-allocation puzzle with useful combos between symbols
Good solo mode and quick setup/teardown
Captures the core race-to-intersect tension of the original in a smaller package
criticised: Feels thin and repetitive after several plays, less depth than the base game
Very little player interaction beyond a shared dice pool
Some find the paper-and-pencil execution fiddly with the erasable sheets/pens
Comparisons to the original often favor the original for long-term replayability

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play, minor competition over shared dice

scoring.why: The winner is whoever first makes their fame and money markers meet on the two opposing tracks, driven by efficient dice use each round

_name: Rajas of the Ganges: The Dice Charmers
